newsitem.title: USA: U S West Comms still backs FY97 EPS view.
newsitem.headline: U S West Comms still backs FY97 EPS view.

text.p: U S West Communications Group remains comfortable with the current consensus earnings estimate for the 1997 year, its chief financial officer said.
"We are still comfortable with the current consensus estimate on the Street," CFO Allan Spies said in a call with analysts when asked if he saw earnings accelerating in 1997.
The current consensus for the 1997 year projects U S West Communications earnings at $2.54 per share versus $2.44 per share in 1996, according to First Call.
In addition, the U S West executive said the company was not in active merger talks with any party.

Spies was responding to an analyst's question on whether U S West saw new strategic opportunities after the U.S. Justice Department's go-ahead late Thursday to the mega-merger of Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp.

Baby Bell stocks were up broadly Friday morning on the news, analysts said. Bell Atlantic jumped 4-1/2 to 63-1/4. NYNEX swelled 4 to 48-3/8. Ameritech Corp rose 3-1/8 points to 59-3/4. BellSouth Corp gained 2-3/4 to 44.
GTE Corp added 1-3/4 to 45-1/8 and newly merged SBC Communications Inc rose 1-3/8 to 51-7/8. U S West shares lagged near the back of the pack, at 32-7/8, up 1-1/2.

Spies said he still sees overall earnings growth in the four to six percent range for the 1997 year, despite an 11.5 percent rise in earnings per share during the first quarter of 1997, results for which the company released earlier Friday.
First quarter net earnings of $0.68 per share exceeded the First Call consensus estimate of $0.65 per share. The comparable figure in the 1996 first quarter was $0.61 a share.
Spies said he expected full-year earnings to be dampened by dilution associated with the construction of new wireless networks and the backend-loaded effects of competition later in the year.
He also said he remained committed to core earnings growth of eight to 10 percent.
"Absent a significant regulatory shift, we remain comfortable with the consensus estimate for the 1997 year," Spies said in concluding comments at the end of the conference call late Friday morning.
